tools.name: internet_status
tools.description: The live status of the whole internet: a one-sentence answer, every watched service (Cloudflare, AWS, Google Workspace, Discord, PlayStation Network, OpenAI, GitHub...) with its state and its group, and the open security incidents with what to do. Refreshed every 5 minutes.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: The open incidents (critical flaws, big outages, supply-chain attacks), worst first, each with its impact, what to do, the affected packages and products, and its page.

tools.name: events_since
tools.description: What changed since a date, oldest first: incidents created, updated or resolved, and big services going down or coming back. Keep `next` and pass it as `since` next time to watch.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: One incident by its id (as list_incidents or internet_status give it, like 2026-10-14-nextjs-rce), open or resolved.

tools.name: check_stack
tools.description: Checks a project's dependencies and a person's apps. Every package with an exact version (as a lockfile pins it) is checked against every known flaw (OSV.dev, CISA's exploited list), and the incidents this site explains come first; a range, no version, or an app is only compared with those incidents

tools.name: check_repo
tools.description: Checks a public GitHub repo: every package its lockfiles pin at its latest commit, in every folder and 14 ecosystems (npm, PyPI, crates.io, Go, Maven, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist, Pub, Swift, Hex, Hackage, CRAN, Julia), against every known flaw.
